title: How to organise the primary workbench | Garage
description:
The one surface in the house where things get fixed, glued, cut, and assembled.

This is the Primary Workbench in the Garage. About 60-90 min.

WHAT DONE LOOKS LIKE
A bare bench top holding only the vise and the task light, one tray with the current job in it, clamps racked on the rail, and swept concrete visible under the bench.

THE SIX PASSES
Sort: Clear the top down to bare wood.
Straighten: Give the vise its own corner and keep a full arm's length of open top in front of it, because that is the spac
Shine: Vacuum sawdust and metal filings out of the bench dog holes and the seam where the top meets the back wall, th
Safety: Check the bench outlet and the task light cord for nicks, and confirm you can plug the sander in without a lea
Standardize: Tape a photo of the cleared bench, vise and task light and nothing else, on the wall directly behind it at eye
Sustain: A project is not over when the glue sets.

THE STANDARD YOU LEAVE BEHIND
The bench ends every session bare except the vise and the task light.

Full written steps for this zone, free:
https://6s-success.com/zones/garage-the-primary-workbench.html

6S Success turns Lean's six-S method into something you can actually do in a house: Sort, Straighten, Shine, Safety, Standardize, Sustain. One small zone at a time, finished in one session, and it stays finished.
